Market stance

The group turns from defensive to bounce-hunting after a wild election-day tape — Sean warns against shorting into the 200-day line while still expecting lower prices in the coming weeks, Prof smells a bottom as the Nasdaq bounces 400 points, and iain counters with QQQ down another ~2% after hours, so the bounce is unconfirmed and no clean qualifier fires today.

Key watches

Catalysts

  • U.S. midterm elections, Tue 11/3 — results landing overnight — Enrich's election-night posts: Democrats favored in his 7 key Senate races, and solar (FSLR/RUN/TAN) as the foreshadowing sector; his claim that Democratic leadership bodes well for solar is his, unverified here
  • QQQ after hours, Tue night — iain reports QQQ down another ~2% after hours (no price stated); Prof's 400-point Nasdaq bounce and red VIX futures point the other way into Wednesday
  • AMD earnings — DiCarlo's Silver Bullet setup into the print, then “bounced to perfection”; he promises a video tomorrow
  • Enrich's 11/4 watchlist — upside: BE, CRDO, FSLR; downside: DELL, CIEN, CAT, MU, SNDK, CRWV; plus solar (FSLR/RUN/TAN) on a multi-month radar
  • Venu's base list — MIR, FISV, GPK, WING flagged as quietly preparing for potential uptrends; FISV (+12.46%) and GPK (+21.22%) already jumped Tuesday, so neither is a chase

Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
A wild election-day window: Tuesday's close was green for most of the board, but the group's posts describe the tape underneath it, not the close. Sean supplies the process read: build the watchlist during the correction but do not buy it yet — a stock holding up better than the market is not a buy signal on its own in this tape — and now that the market is testing the 200-day line, he warns against shorting into it while still expecting lower prices in the coming weeks: an oversold bounce spot, not a bottom. Prof supplies the tape read in the other direction: the Nasdaq down 3% from earlier highs, then a 400-point bounce, red VIX futures, and “This week we're gonna bottom. I can smell it.” iain supplies the counterweight and the short side: QQQ down another ~2% after hours after he asked for real fear and capitulation, and a standing frame to short weak bounces into declining 9/21 EMAs in SPCX, SKHY, DRAM and BE, risking the high of day. Enrich supplies the split tape for Wednesday: BE, CRDO and FSLR upside; DELL, CIEN, CAT, MU, SNDK and CRWV downside; solar on a multi-month radar after the election read; and a Texas warning for AI/data-center names, with IREN's 2.7 GW Texas footprint named and NBIS explicitly noted as having no Texas data centers. Venu supplies the base read: MIR, FISV, GPK and WING quietly preparing for potential uptrends, plus GOOGL testing ~$270 support with his $204 long-term line below. DiCarlo supplies the earnings read: AMD's Silver Bullet setup into the print, then “bounced to perfection.” Remz posts nothing tradeable in this window — “Puts sold and heading to bed” with no name or level. Your process gives no clean qualifier today either: MIR sits at its 3-month high but 54.39% under its 52-week high; FISV and GPK already jumped 12.46% and 21.22% on Tuesday, so both are extended, not entries; BE and CRDO carry upside listings but sit below every short average; and the rest of the tape is tests to survive — SPY on its 30-week line at 751.38, GOOGL's $270 test, AMD's bounce still below its 30-week line. The discipline is in the framing: hold-or-fail levels (SPY 751.38, GOOGL 270, AMD 495.10/456.16, BE 239.92/200.09) decide Wednesday, while the downside list and iain's short list are called out as shorts and avoids, not entries.

  • Badge key: Setup describes structure only (green = constructive, amber = pending confirmation, red = broken/extended/avoid). Coverage counts the traders behind a name and is always gray — “Chart only” means no trader mentioned it and implies nothing about the setup. The stage pill next to each ticker (30-week MA basis) is the only place a stage label appears; it is kept out of the prose and the setup badges, and traders' own quoted words are exempt.
  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels. SPCX, SKHY and DRAM show no invalidation row: they are short ideas, and there is no long thesis below to invalidate.
  • Trader charts: none embedded this edition. No trader posted a retrievable chart image for a covered name in the visible posts this window, so no trader chart is embedded rather than risking a wrong one.
  • Chart verification gate: every plotted line's endpoint was checked against levels.json before the HTML was built — all computable lines passed within 0.5%. The 30-week MA is a true trailing mean over full 30-week windows only.
